summary: This program stores a price with cents in a double, then converts it to an int so only the whole dollars remain. It shows narrowing casting: turning a larger type into a smaller one, which discards the fractional part.

lines.text: A double holds numbers with a decimal point, so it can store the full price of 100.30 including the cents.

lines.code: int adPrice = (int) price; // narrow casting from double to int
lines.text: The (int) in front of price is a cast that forces the double into an int. Java will not do this automatically because information is lost: the .30 is chopped off, not rounded, leaving 100.
Joining text to a number with + turns the number into text, so the output reads as a single sentence with the rounded-down dollar amount.
